answer: Tie each identity to a physical device. Phones and security keys hold a chip whose key was certified at the factory and cannot be extracted. The registry accepts one identity per certified chip and checks the manufacturer's certificate chain. Emulators on an island of rented servers carry no such certificate, so every fake needs a real purchased device, one more pearl bought at full price. A prism splits light, but no one can split one chip's key into a hundred names.
